provenance.paper_title: Modeling Dynamic Environments with Scene Graph Memory

representation_paths.memory_component: agent accumulated observations of rooms, objects, and temporal relations in dynamic environments

evidence.paraphrase: Scene Graph Memory aggregates observed nodes and edges with time references; NEP predicts likely object locations. NEP extracts information from SGM to predict object locations and guide efficient search; explicit retrieval is model-mediated.

During operation, Scene Graph Memory applies fixed-rule correction of stored state to agent accumulated observations of rooms, objects, and temporal relations in dynamic environments; the memory state changes while the governing update policy remains fixed.

evidence.section: Full paper: Algorithm 1 Dynamic House Simulator Algorithm
evidence.paraphrase: SGM is updated as the agent observes subsets of the changing scene graph over time. For Scene Graph Memory, this specifically supports relinking or reindexing of stored items of agent accumulated observations of rooms, objects, and temporal relations in dynamic environments.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 3): During inference, the operative memory component (agent accumulated observations of rooms, objects, and temporal relations in dynamic environments) changes through fixed-rule correction of stored state, relinking or reindexing of stored items; the governing policy remains fixed, and any learning reported by the paper occurs before deployment. Training-time learning, when present, was not counted as T3.
